## Workflow

A range becomes a running range in two commands on a prepared host:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
inspect-ranges render range.yaml -o bundle/
inspect-ranges up bundle/
```

A range declaring guest content needs a matching build first: your own ([Building Ranges](building.qmd)), or a published one that the first `inspect eval` (or an explicit `pull`) fetches automatically ([Distribution](distribution.qmd)). Images need no preparation either way: bare `image:` names resolve digest-verified on first use ([Images](images.qmd)). `inspect-ranges doctor` checks the host first and prints fixes for whatever is missing.

Each stage consumes only the verified output of the one before it: `render` emits a digest-manifested bundle, and `up` refuses to act on anything whose digests do not verify.

Moving builds and images between machines (`push`, `pull`, `mirror`, `publish`) is [Distribution](distribution.qmd); the deployment-shape recipes are [Images](images.qmd). This page walks the lifecycle; complete option listings for every command are in the [CLI reference](reference/index.qmd#cli).

## `up`

`inspect-ranges up <bundle>` realizes a rendered bundle into a running, ready range: every manifest digest verifies first (tampered, incomplete, unlisted-file, or path-escaping bundles refuse; `boot.json` is shape-validated before any value reaches a command), image digests re-verify against the cache, then the hardened range container comes up on the bundle's own compose project, guests boot per `boot.json`, and readiness waits on every guest (daemon answering over vsock, then `cloud-init status --wait` succeeding, probed over the control channel). The hardened non-root-QEMU range image is built automatically and is required; there is no bypass.

`up --from-spec range.yaml` composes render into a temporary bundle first. `--uplink-network` supplies the deployment uplink for ranges that request egress. A second `up` of an identical bundle refuses, naming the running project and the exact `down` command.

On failure, the error names the stage and guest, the affected guests' serial console logs are pulled into the project state directory (`~/.local/state/inspect-ranges/projects/<project>/`, next to the JSONL stage log), and the project tears down unless `--keep` is passed.

## `down`

`inspect-ranges down <project>` tears down by recorded ownership (compose labels and deterministic names), never by live process state: it works from any process, after any crash, and twice in a row. `down --all` sweeps every `ir-` project discovered from the ownership registry, container labels, and volume names, attempting all of them and aggregating any failures. The sweep cannot tell a crashed project from one mid-boot, so run it only when nothing on the host should be live. A failed removal keeps the ownership record so a retry can still find the project.

## `shell`

`inspect-ranges shell <project> [guest]` opens an interactive shell on a guest of a running range: a tmux session inside the guest, driven over the range's control channel, so it needs no SSH, no guest listener, and works on fully isolated networks. The guest defaults to the range's attacker when it has exactly one; `--session` names the tmux session (the same name reattaches, and sessions survive detach); `--user` picks the guest identity (default: the daemon identity, root on Linux); `--cast <path>` records the attach as a local asciicast. Detach with `Ctrl-]`.

This is an operator surface for ranges booted with `up` (trying tasks by hand, debugging guest state and images). A project booted by the Inspect sandbox provider refuses by recorded origin, so an eval sample can never acquire an interactive operator mid-run. Guest output is treated as untrusted: display sequences pass to your terminal, but clipboard writes, palette programming, and device-control strings are filtered out. Linux guests only (the session is tmux). One known seam: the attach paints the current visible screen and then streams new output, so a full-screen program already mid-flight may need a redraw (`Ctrl-L`) to render cleanly.

## `applier`

`inspect-ranges applier --socket <path>` serves the host side of a separated topology (driver on one machine, range host on another) on a unix socket, relaying guest control traffic; see [Range Host](topology.qmd). It runs the doctor readiness subset at startup and refuses to serve an unhealthy host; drivers reach it via `INSPECT_RANGES_HOST=uds:<path>`.

## `reaper`

`inspect-ranges reaper` reclaims expired host leases from on-disk state in one sweep (`--interval <s>` runs it as a daemon). It reclaims on expiry alone, never probing liveness; a failed teardown frees nothing and the next sweep retries. See [Range Host](topology.qmd) for the lease contract.

## `doctor`

`inspect-ranges doctor` checks the host (virtualization devices, docker versions, networking sysctls, image tooling) plus four surface groups:

- **Realizer**: the hardened range image, the daemon artifact, and the Go toolchain (warnings, not failures: `up` builds the image on demand and `daemon-bundle` publishes the artifact once per fleet).

- **Provider and host**: entry-point registration, goldens, CID and host lease registry health with an expired-leases hint naming the reaper, lease origins this machine can resolve, and the selected backend itself: the applier socket probe when `INSPECT_RANGES_HOST` points at one, or resolution plus the bundle's own probe for a [registered backend](topology.qmd#registering-a-backend).

- **Evidence**: knob validity, a writability probe of a configured sink, and a warning when evidence resolves to instance-local storage (see [Evidence](evidence.qmd)).

- **Build**: builds/recipe cache writability, recorded manifests and cached recipe bundles still parse, and whether a build nameserver is derivable from this host's resolv.conf (see [Building Ranges](building.qmd)).

`--fix-script` emits the shell commands for whatever failed.

::: {.callout-note}
## Current Boundaries

`up` realizes cold-boot bundles only: checkpoint instantiation is planned later work. `provisioning`, `services`, and `vulnerabilities` realize through [`build`](building.qmd): a range declaring them refuses every content-consuming verb (`range-not-built`) until a matching build manifest exists, and boots its captured realized images once one does. `users`, `misconfigurations`, and `data` realize through `build` like the content sections, as do `roles`, `defense`, Active Directory, telemetry-bearing postures, and `scheduled_activity` (installed as persistent units in the captured images), so nothing boots with silently missing content. Windows guests are supported (goldens derive locally with `images derive-windows`). Bundles are trusted operator input: verification proves integrity, not provenance (bundle signing is planned as part of image-distribution work).
:::
